rows: Despair, widely: every torch in the camp gutters
Fear, steadily: the door flinches open and stays open
Long range; arrives a moment later
Love, far: the surge leaps to a distant hay cart
Spreads to everything around the target
Hope, wholly: every vine along the edge reaches across
Unmaking: Hate, slowly: the wolf's hate drains unnoticed
Despair, fleetingly: the torch gutters and you slip into the dark
Fear, suddenly: the door flinches open, then slams and jams
Joy, deeply: one door brightens, not the shrine around it

items: Any emotion can be an adverb, including the verb's own; a verb's opposite as adverb cancels into a lucidity dispel.
Adverbs chain after the separator (Hate Hate · Far Steadily). The chain cap is shared between verb and adverbs.
Repeating an adverb intensifies it (far, very far, farthest). Opposite adverbs cancel into lucidity. Clashing manners play out in order.
An adverb costs a little of its own emotion, always a minor part of the composition.
